page: Microsoft Azure L24aos_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, it features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU runs at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a massive 17,279 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities. No GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 25%. Text processing performance is also strong. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. Notably, the instance achieves top-tier performance in LLM inference text generation using small 135M models, reaching 338.79 tokens per second. However, it exhibits weak performance for prompt processing on large 70B models, indicating a clear tradeoff when handling massive parameter sets.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the L24aos_v4 provides high resource density, combining substantial memory capacity with an exceptionally large local storage allocation. This makes it highly suitable for data-intensive workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. The server is well-suited for large-scale database hosting, memory-intensive data processing, text processing pipelines, and lightweight language model inference.
